stripText.remove: (In each diagram a distant tree sends rays to a concave mirror which reflects them onto a screen. In A and B the incoming rays are not truly parallel and the convergence is poor. In C the parallel rays converge low on the screen. In D the incoming rays are clearly parallel and converge to a single sharp point on a correctly placed screen.)

The figures show: (W) protractor with its straight (diameter) edge laid along the mirror surface, near the incident ray; (X) protractor with its straight edge laid along the normal, near the incident ray; (Y) protractor with its straight edge laid along the mirror surface, near the reflected ray; (Z) protractor with its straight edge laid along the normal, near the reflected ray.

In A the ray passes straight through the slab without bending. In B the ray bends towards the normal on entering, travels through, and bends away from the normal on leaving so that the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray (laterally shifted). In C the ray passes straight through without bending. In D the ray bends on entering but the emergent ray is not parallel to the incident ray.

The incident ray is parallel to the principal axis (C and F are marked on the axis, P is the pole). In (a) the reflected ray passes through the focus F. In (b) the reflected ray passes through the centre of curvature (2F). In (c) the ray is reflected straight back along the same path. In (d) the reflected ray crosses the axis between the focus F and the pole P.

The incident ray comes from the upper-left and passes through the focus F on the object (near) side before reaching a convex lens (optical centre O). In (a) the emergent ray is reflected straight back. In (b) the emergent ray goes upward, diverging away from the axis. In (c) the ray passes straight through the optical centre undeviated. In (d) the emergent ray travels parallel to the principal axis.

In diagram A the parallel rays pass through device X and converge to a sharp, inverted image of the tree on a screen placed on the far side of X (opposite the incoming rays). In diagram B the rays pass through X but the tree image shown on the far-side screen is upright (erect).
